pathways.title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
pathways.reagentNote: Draw the alkyl halide and alkoxide as disconnected structures
pathways.shortExplanation: An alkoxide displaces the leaving group by SN2 to form an ether. Methyl and primary halides are best; secondary halides can undergo competing E2.
limitations: Secondary halides can undergo substantial E2; tertiary halides are excluded.
SN2 inversion is explicitly encoded when the reacting carbon is stereogenic.

pathways.title: E2 with an Unhindered Alkoxide
pathways.reagentNote: Small, unhindered strong base → Zaitsev-favored E2
pathways.shortExplanation: A strong, relatively unhindered alkoxide removes a beta hydrogen as the leaving group departs. The more substituted Zaitsev alkene is normally favored.

selectivityAssessment.label: Major product (qualitative)
selectivityAssessment.basis: Zaitsev rule: with small strong bases (hydroxide, methoxide, ethoxide) E2 gives mainly the more substituted alkene (LibreTexts, Elimination by the E2 mechanism; UCLA Illustrated Glossary of Organic Chemistry, Hofmann's rule: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane with methoxide gives 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product; Reusch, MSU: 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane with methoxide gives 80% of the tetrasubstituted alkene). This is the more substituted alkene. Qualitative preference, not a measured ratio; E/Z geometry within a constitution is not ranked.

limitations: The handler generates E/Z for common acyclic disubstituted alkenes, but does not yet determine anti-periplanar conformer availability or general trisubstituted/tetrasubstituted alkene geometry.
Secondary substrates can show competing SN2.
